about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Lemon Yoghurt Loaf Slices
recipes.summary: A moist, tangy loaf with a thin lemon glaze, cut into thick slices for the lunchbox or afternoon tea.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 22 x 12cm loaf tin with baking paper. Whisk the eggs, sugar and lemon zest for 2 minutes until pale.
Whisk in the yoghurt, olive oil and 2 tbsp of the lemon juice, then fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 minutes, until golden and a skewer in the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then lift out onto a rack.
Stir the remaining lemon juice into the icing sugar until smooth, then drizzle over the warm loaf. Let the glaze set for 15 minutes before cutting into 10 slices.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Chewy Oat and Sultana Cookies
recipes.summary: Soft-centred oat cookies with plump sultanas and brown sugar, ready from bowl to biscuit tin in half an hour.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper. Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until fluffy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, oats and sultanas until a thick dough forms.
Roll heaped tablespoons (about 40g each) into 18 balls, place 5cm apart and flatten slightly.
Bake for 12 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Lemon Coconut Slice
recipes.summary: A shortbread base under a chewy lemon and coconut topping made with condensed milk, cut into small squares.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Mix the flour, sugar and melted butter, press firmly into the tin and bake for 20 minutes until pale golden.
Stir the condensed milk, coconut, lemon zest, lemon juice and egg together until combined.
Spread over the hot base and bake for a further 20 minutes, until the top is golden and set.
Cool completely in the tin, then cut into 16 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: wash your hands after handling raw egg and make sure the topping is baked until set.

recipes.title: Mixed Berry Oat Squares
recipes.summary: A buttery oat crumble pressed around a jammy mixed berry centre, cut into squares that travel well.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Mix the oats, flour, brown sugar and baking powder, then stir in the melted butter until crumbly.
Press two-thirds of the mixture firmly into the tin and bake for 10 minutes, until the edges are just set.
Toss the berries with the caster sugar, cornflour and lemon juice, spread over the base and scatter the remaining crumble on top.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the top is golden and the berries are bubbling. Cool completely in the tin, then cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Cheddar and Chive Scones
recipes.summary: Tall, tender savoury scones with sharp cheese and fresh chives, best eaten warm with butter.

items: 1 cup grated vegetarian hard cheese, cheddar style (100g)
1 cup milk (250ml), plus 1 tbsp for glazing

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour, salt and mustard powder with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in 3/4 of the cheese and the chives, then add the milk and mix with a knife to a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Turn onto a floured bench and pat out to 3cm thick. Cut 12 rounds with a 6cm cutter and place them close together on the tray.
Brush with milk, top with the remaining cheese and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and deep golden. Cool for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 scone. Best on the day; freeze for up to 2 months and reheat at 160°C fan for 8 minutes.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Apple and Walnut Scones
recipes.summary: Scones studded with grated apple, walnuts and cinnamon, soft inside with a golden top.

items: 3/4 cup milk (185ml), plus 1 tbsp for glazing

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and cinnamon until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Squeeze the grated apple in your fist to remove extra juice, then stir it through with the walnuts.
Add the milk and mix with a knife to a soft dough. Pat out to 3cm thick on a floured bench and cut 12 rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Place close together on the tray, brush with milk and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and golden. Cool for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 scone. Best on the day; freeze for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Fruit Scones with Jam and Cream
recipes.summary: Classic sultana scones served with strawberry jam and softly whipped cream, a proper afternoon tea.

items: 1 cup milk (250ml), plus 1 tbsp for glazing
100ml thickened cream, whipped to soft peaks

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour and sugar until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the sultanas.
Add the milk and mix with a knife to a soft dough. Pat out to 3cm thick on a floured bench and cut 12 rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Place close together on the tray, brush with milk and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and golden. Cool for 5 minutes under a tea towel.
Split each scone and serve with a spoonful of jam and a dollop of cream.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 scone with jam and cream. Scones are best on the day; freeze them for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Scone Scrolls
recipes.summary: No-yeast scone dough rolled up with cinnamon sugar and finished with a thin icing, ready in under an hour.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Rub the cold butter into the flour until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the 1 cup of milk to make a soft dough.
Roll the dough on a floured bench into a 25 x 40cm rectangle. Spread with the soft butter and scatter with the brown sugar and cinnamon.
Roll up from the long side, trim the ends and cut into 10 even pieces. Pack them cut side up in the tin.
Bake for 18 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Stir the icing sugar with the 1 tbsp of milk and drizzle over the warm scrolls.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 scroll. Best on the day; keeps 2 days airtight.

recipes.title: Custard Tarts
recipes.summary: Crisp shortcrust cases holding a barely-set nutmeg custard, baked in a muffin tin.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar until it looks like breadcrumbs. Mix in the egg yolk and enough cold water to form a dough, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the pastry to 3mm thick, cut 12 rounds with a 9cm cutter and press into a greased 12-hole muffin tin. Bake for 10 minutes until pale and dry.
Reduce the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Whisk the eggs, sugar, milk and vanilla together and pour into the cases, then dust with nutmeg.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the custard is just set with a slight wobble in the centre. Cool in the tin for 15 minutes and chill before serving.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tart. Plus 30 minutes chilling the pastry. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Food safety: bake the custard until set, wash your hands after handling raw egg, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Apricot Jam Tarts
recipes.summary: Little buttery pastry cases filled with bubbling strawberry jam, a party plate favourite.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar until it looks like breadcrumbs. Mix in the egg yolk and cold water to form a dough, wrap and chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the pastry to 3mm thick, cut 12 rounds with a 8cm cutter and press into a greased 12-hole tart or muffin tin.
Spoon 1 tbsp jam into each case, filling them only two-thirds full as the jam bubbles up.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the jam is bubbling. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, as the jam is very hot.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tart. Plus 20 minutes chilling the pastry. Keeps 4 days airtight.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling the raw egg yolk.

recipes.title: Lemon Curd Tartlets
recipes.summary: Crisp pastry cases filled with a tangy, silky home-made lemon curd.
steps: Rub the 125g butter into the flour and icing sugar, mix in the egg yolk and water to a dough, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the pastry to 3mm, cut 12 rounds with a 8cm cutter, press into a 12-hole tin and bake for 12 minutes until golden. Cool.
Whisk the eggs, extra yolk, sugar, zest and juice in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring for 8 minutes until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Do not let it boil.
Off the heat, whisk in the 60g butter until smooth, then spoon the hot curd into the cases. Chill for 1 hour until set.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tartlet. Plus 30 minutes chilling the pastry and 1 hour setting. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Food safety: cook the curd until thick and hot, wash your hands after handling raw egg, and refrigerate within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Mixed Berry Almond Friands
recipes.summary: Light, moist almond cakes made with egg whites and berries in the middle.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Whisk the egg whites lightly with a fork until just frothy.
Stir in the icing sugar, almond meal, flour and orange zest, then mix in the melted butter until smooth.
Divide among the holes, push 2 or 3 berries into each and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and springy to the touch.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 friand. Keeps 3 days airtight.
Food safety: bake until golden and set; wash your hands and bowls after handling raw egg white.

recipes.title: Orange and Sesame Seed Muffins
recipes.summary: Bright, citrusy muffins with a crunch of sesame seeds, mixed in one bowl.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases. Mix the flour, sugar, sesame seeds and orange zest in a large bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter and orange juice together, tip into the dry mix and fold until just combined; a few lumps are fine.
Divide among the cases and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days airtight; freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Mixed Berry Coconut Muffins
recipes.summary: Tender muffins with tart mixed berries and desiccated coconut, with no mixer needed.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases. Mix the flour, coconut and sugar in a large bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk and melted butter together, tip into the dry mix and fold until just combined.
Gently fold in the frozen berries, divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days airtight; freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Carrot Cake Squares with Cream Cheese Icing
recipes.summary: Spiced carrot and walnut cake topped with tangy icing, cut into party-size squares.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Whisk the eggs, brown sugar and oil together, then stir in the carrot and walnuts.
Fold in the flour and cinnamon until just combined. Pour into the tin and bake for 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool completely in the tin. Beat the cream cheese, butter and icing sugar until smooth, spread over the cake and chill for 20 minutes.
Cut into 16 squares with a hot, dry knife.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares. Plus 20 minutes chilling. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.
Food safety: wash your hands after handling raw egg and keep the iced cake in the fridge.

recipes.title: Honey Oat Flapjacks
recipes.summary: Chewy, golden oat bars sweetened with honey and brown sugar, with just five ingredients.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Melt the butter, sugar and honey in a saucepan over low heat for 3 minutes until smooth.
Stir in the oats and salt until every oat is coated.
Press firmly into the tin and bake for 25 minutes, until golden around the edges but still soft in the centre.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 12 bars; they firm up as they cool.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey). Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 5 days airtight.

recipes.title: Fudgy Brownie Squares
recipes.summary: Dense chocolate squares with a crackly top and a fudgy middle.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Melt the chocolate and butter together over low heat, stirring, then cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk the sugar and eggs into the chocolate mixture until glossy.
Fold in the flour and cocoa until just combined, then pour into the tin.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the top is set and cracked but the centre is still slightly soft. Cool completely in the tin and cut into 16 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares. Keeps 4 days airtight.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Shortbread Fingers
recipes.summary: Pale, crumbly Scottish-style shortbread that melts in the mouth.
steps: Heat the oven to 140°C fan (160°C conventional) and line a 20 x 30cm tin with baking paper. Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale.
Stir in the flour and cornflour to form a soft dough, then press evenly into the tin and prick all over with a fork.
Bake for 30 minutes, until pale golden at the edges; it should not colour much.
Cut into 24 fingers while hot, then cool completely in the tin.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 fingers. Keeps 2 weeks airtight.

recipes.title: Ginger Crunch Squares
recipes.summary: A crisp ginger base topped with a sticky, sweet ginger icing, a classic bakery slice.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Beat the 125g butter and caster sugar until pale, then stir in the flour, baking powder and 1 tbsp ginger.
Press firmly into the tin and bake for 20 minutes, until golden.
While it bakes, melt the 80g butter and golden syrup in a saucepan, then stir in the icing sugar and remaining ginger until smooth.
Pour the icing over the hot base, cool completely and cut into 20 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares. Keeps 5 days airtight.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Sugar Doughnut Muffins
recipes.summary: Soft muffins brushed with butter and rolled in cinnamon sugar, tasting like a baked doughnut.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Whisk the egg, milk and the 80g melted butter together.
Stir in the flour and 1/2 cup sugar until just combined and divide among the holes.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden and springy. Cool for 5 minutes.
Mix the coating sugar and cinnamon. Brush each warm muffin all over with the melted butter, then roll in the cinnamon sugar.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. Best on the day.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Soft-Baked Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.summary: Thick cookies with crisp edges, a soft centre and plenty of dark chocolate.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper. Beat the butter and both sugars for 3 minutes until fluffy, then beat in the egg, yolk and vanilla.
Stir in the flour and bicarbonate of soda, then fold through the chocolate chips.
Roll 24 balls (about 40g each), place 6cm apart on the trays and bake for 11 minutes, swapping trays halfway, until the edges are set and the centres look slightly underdone.
Rest on the tray for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Keeps 5 days airtight.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Gingerbread Biscuits
recipes.summary: Spiced golden syrup biscuits that hold their shape for cutting and decorating.
steps: Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the golden syrup and egg. Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, ginger and cinnamon to form a dough, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper.
Roll the dough 4mm thick on a floured bench and cut out 30 shapes with a 7cm cutter, re-rolling the offcuts.
Bake for 10 minutes, until firm at the edges and lightly browned. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes, then on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 biscuits. Plus 30 minutes chilling. Keeps 2 weeks airtight.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Oat Bars
recipes.summary: No-bake chewy bars of oats, peanut butter, honey and sultanas, set in the fridge.
steps: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Warm the peanut butter and honey in a saucepan over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring until smooth and runny.
Off the heat, stir in the oats, sultanas and salt until evenly coated.
Press very firmly into the tin with the back of a spoon so the bars hold together.
Chill for 1 hour until firm, then cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey). Contains peanuts and gluten. Per serving: 1 bar. Plus 1 hour chilling. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.
